note: Dsus2 and Dsus4 as one finger off or on a D: the shapes, a bar of each in downstrokes, then Dsus4 as the bar before D at the end of a phrase. One file for the drill at two levels (the beginner copy and the sus groove are folded in): the words are the same, the beginner choice moves 60 to 70 bpm and the intermediate one 60 to 90. Open shapes, so no key move.

exercise.title: Dsus2 and Dsus4 around D
exercise.why: Dsus2 is D with one finger lifted and Dsus4 is D with one finger added, both on the high e string, so one finger turns a still D into a moving part.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret each chord as shown. Change from D to Dsus2 and back, then from D to Dsus4 and back.
Practice until only the one finger moves and the rest of your hand stays still.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat.
If the finger comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.

Press a chord box below to see the two new shapes, G and A. Then press Play under them to start the metronome. Strum the pattern in the boxes: after G and A, Dsus4 holds for a bar and falls back to D in the next.
Listen for how the bar of Dsus4 leans towards D.
